newsitem.title: FINLAND: ASKO'S UPONOR UPBEAT ON PLASTIC PIPES.
newsitem.headline: ASKO'S UPONOR UPBEAT ON PLASTIC PIPES.

text.p: Finnish plastic pipes maker Oy Uponor Ab, a unit of Asko Oy, said on Thursday that the worldwide outlook for growth in plastic pipes was good.

"Prospects for growth in the plastic pipe industry are reasonably good worldwide," Uponor said in a statement reporting 1996 earnings before extras and taxes up to 245 million markka from 193 million in 1995.

"Increasing environmental awareness and mounting concern for safeguarding water resources will push up demand for durable, leak-proof pipe systems," Uponor's president Heikki Mairinoja said in the statement.

"The economic outlook for the immediate future is promising too. Europe is looking forward to a period of relatively strong growth while the housing construction sector in the United States is expected to remain buoyant," Uponor said.
Uponor's 1996 net sales rose to 3.76 billion markka in 1996 from 3.59 billion in 1995. Operating profit rose to 296 million markka in 1996 from 265 million a year ago.
"The group' good performance was primarily the result of average or above average levels of demand in all its main markets combined with stable plastic resin prices," Uponor said.
On February 25, Asko reported group 1996 earnings up 26 percent on 1995 to 401 million markka.
